criteria.criterion: Wherever the guard runs today (around every session, gate and check, including the base gates at acceptance and the gate review), .git/config is compared by its own entries — keys and values, include directives as entries, never the files they include — not by its bytes; the git hooks guard is unchanged.
criteria.evidence: internal/driver/gitguard.go configEntries reads `git config --list -z --no-includes` and splits each entry with strings.Cut(e, "\n"); a key with no value (`[core] fsmonitor`, true) and a key with an empty value (`fsmonitor =`) both yield val "", so the entries are not compared faithfully. Call sites are unchanged, hooks guard unchanged.

criteria.criterion: An entry whose key matches an ignore pattern is left out of both sides. The built-in pattern is branch.*.vscode-merge-base and is always applied. A pattern matches the key as git config --list prints it (section and variable lowercased, subsection as written), and * matches any run of characters, dots included.
criteria.evidence: internal/gitcfg/gitcfg.go Match/Ignored, BuiltinIgnore always prepended in snapshotGit; TestMatch covers dots, subsections and case

criteria.criterion: run.git-config-ignore is a list config key (environment VLOOP_RUN_GIT_CONFIG_IGNORE, comma-separated) whose patterns are added to the built-in one; it never removes the built-in pattern. vloop config get and config list show it.
criteria.evidence: internal/config/config.go Keys entry; config list tests in internal/cli/config_test.go and cmd/vloop/e2e_test.go; TestRunGitConfigIgnoreFromEnvironment

criteria.criterion: A pattern is protected when its text before the first * (all of it, if it has none) and one of core., filter., include., includeif. is a prefix of the other. vloop config set run.git-config-ignore with a protected pattern (alone or in a list) exits 2, writes nothing, and prints exactly `vloop: run.git-config-ignore: <pattern> would ignore <section>.* — the guard must see it`, <pattern> the offending pattern itself (core.* for the list gitlens.*,core.*), <section> the first of core, filter, include, includeif, in that order, it collides with: *, c*, core.* and filter.lfs.* are refused; gitlens.* and branch.*.vscode-merge-base are not.
criteria.evidence: gitcfg.Protected and TestProtected; TestGitConfigIgnoreRefusesProtectedPatterns asserts the message, UsageError and no file written

criteria.criterion: vloop run with a protected pattern in VLOOP_RUN_GIT_CONFIG_IGNORE or in the config file refuses with exit 1 and the same line, before any session runs.
criteria.evidence: internal/cli/run.go config.Get after ResolveBudgets; TestRunGitConfigProtectedPatternRefused (env only; file path covered by sourceErr unit test)

criteria.criterion: Any other entry added, removed or changed halts with exit 9 and exactly `vloop: <who> changed .git/config (<key>[, <key>…][ and <n> more]) — nothing was committed; restore it, then re-run`: at most three keys, sorted, then how many more; <who> is what it is today (work, review, plan, the gate review, the gate of T5, the check go, …). An ignored key never appears among the named keys and never halts on its own.
criteria.evidence: gitGuard.changed names sorted keys with 'and n more' and TestRunGitConfigPlanted asserts it, but a change between a bare key (true) and an empty-valued key (`core.fsmonitor =` vs `core.fsmonitor`) is not seen, so an entry changed without halting

criteria.criterion: Violations the review must rule against: a key outside the ignore patterns that changes without halting; an ignored key that halts; a built-in pattern list in the binary that a repository cannot extend; a guard that only checks known-dangerous keys.
criteria.evidence: a key outside the ignore patterns can change (bare <-> empty value, including core.fsmonitor which flips false to true) without halting; values of a multi-valued key are also sorted, so reordering is invisible

criteria.criterion: The pattern matching and the protected-pattern rule are pure functions with committed unit tests that run on every OS, and a committed end-to-end test in cmd/vloop shows a run continuing past an ignored key and halting with the named key otherwise.

Only these existing tests change, and only as the brief states: TestRunGitConfigPlanted (cmd/vloop/run_git_test.go) and the hooks/config subtests of TestWorkedExampleB8 (cmd/vloop/b8_e2e_test.go) expect the key named; TestWorkedExampleEnglishSession (cmd/vloop/e2e_test.go) expects the new key in config list. No other assertion is weakened.
criteria.evidence: diff touches also TestDefaultsEveryRow and TestConfigListDefaults/JSONOrder, but only by adding the new key to the pinned list; no assertion weakened

criteria.criterion: docs/guide/configuration.md lists run.git-config-ignore with its environment name, its built-in pattern and the protected sections; docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated if any help text changed.
criteria.evidence: docs/guide/configuration.md new row; no help text changed

criteria.criterion: No refactor from B15's list (one git wrapper, the env filters, planSHA, driver.counts, the budget keys, the id generators, long functions) is folded in.
criteria.evidence: diff limited to gitguard, gitcfg, config key, run.go check

findings.summary: configEntries cannot tell a valueless key (true) from an empty value: both give "" after strings.Cut, so e.g. core.fsmonitor changing from empty to bare changes meaning without halting; a test for it is missing
values of a repeated key are sorted before comparing, so reordering them (order-significant in git) never halts
